Date: 2027-10-02T09:18:00Z
Subject: Consent evidence and SCCs routing for Enterprise order form

Hi Sophi —

Quick context: procurement asked for two items before they can sign the Order Form so I want to surface them here and align next steps. We have the draft Order Form and MSA redlines in flight but procurement's signoff will require: 

- A short evidence pack showing lawful bases for processing (contractual necessity vs consent) for the product features you plan to enable (particularly file upload + embeddings).
- Confirmation of which SCCs invocation you want (standard EU SCCs v2 with data exporter as controller) and whether you need the Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA).

I've attached a tracked-redline DPA (DPA_RedwoodTrackRedlines_v2.docx) and a skeleton SCCs evidence checklist (SCCs-Evidence-Checklist.xlsx) that maps specific data types and subprocessors. Can you confirm: 

1) Which lawful basis Enterprise will rely on for user-uploaded content?
2) Will Enterprise require us to provide processor-level encryption evidence (KMS/HSM) for regulated datasets?
3) Is the signatory on your side the commercial contact or will Legal need a separate signature line on the Order Form?

If it helps, Ben (cc) can summarize the redline delta and Laura can confirm procurement timeline. Goal: capture the evidence bundle this week so procurement can finalize PO.

Thanks,
Olga
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
Olga Petrov | Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: DPA_RedwoodTrackRedlines_v2.docx (tracked changes), SCCs-Evidence-Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Sophi Patel <sophi.p@enterprisedata.com>

Date: 2027-10-02T14:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Consent evidence and SCCs routing for Enterprise order form

Olga —

Thanks for sending these. Quick answers inline: 

1) Lawful basis: For most product flows we'll rely on contractual necessity for processing of customer files uploaded via our app (we will not require end-user consent flows for those). For a small pilot feature that extracts analytics from user messages we may need separate opt-in — we'll confirm scope by Friday.

2) Encryption: We require evidence that keys are KMS-backed; for datasets marked as "sensitive" we need details on key separation and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK). Please confirm in the evidence pack.

3) Signatory: Commercial will sign the Order Form but Legal will countersign the DPA in parallel. Please include a signature block for both parties on the DPA.

Enterprise Legal (cc) — can you confirm any additional evidence you require for SCCs invocation? We are in an EU region deployment, so TIA likely needed.

Two asks for Redwood:
- Can you populate the attached checklist with the processing categories and the list of subprocessors that will see personal data (even if they are ephemeral)?
- If you have a preferred SCCs + TIA template, please highlight in the redline doc what you are proposing to invoke.

Thanks — Sophi
Sophi Patel
Head of Procurement, Enterprise Data Corp

Attachment stubs: enterprise-internal-legal-ask.pdf (referenced)

Subject: Re: Consent evidence and SCCs routing for Enterprise order form

Team / Sophi —

Summary update and deliverables (per Olga's ask):

1) SCCs & TIA: Recommendation = EU SCCs (Controller-Processor) v2 + Transfer Impact Addendum. Reason: Enterprise is EU-hosted and will be the controller for customer uploads; TIA prudent given downstream subprocessors. We'll mark the TIA as an exhibit to the DPA.

2) Lawful basis: We will document contractual necessity for core upload/processing flows; for the analytics pilot that requires opt-in we'll mark explicit consent in the evidence checklist.

3) KMS/CMK: Karthik confirms CMK is available via our Dedicated offering but requires a one-time engineering enablement (est. 2 weeks). For Enterprise's production timeline we can offer CMK as an optional add-on; in the evidence pack we'll include: key location, rotation policy, and HSM attestation summary (redacted).

4) Subprocessors & data categories: Attached SCCs-Evidence-Checklist.xlsx updated with processing categories (identifiers, content, metadata), and a current subprocessor roster (infra + logging + analytics). We note ephemeral caches are used but not persisted beyond 24 hours (see sheet "cache_retention").

5) Signatures / DocuSign: We'll add a dual signature block to the DPA and expose a DocuSign link for the Order Form + DPA bundle once Enterprise confirms final exhibit language.

Action items: 
- Olga to incorporate the TIA exhibit and the CMK option into the DPA redline (Olga: due EOD 2027-10-04).
- Laura to confirm procurement will accept parallel DPA countersign (Laura: please confirm).
- Sophi / Enterprise Legal to confirm the pilot scope that requires consent by 2027-10-08.

Sophi, attaching the updated checklist and a one-page redline summary (redline summary stub included in the doc comment). If this alignment looks good we will publish the DocuSign package.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
